project-title.title: RudolfVX: A multimodal foundation model for pathology to power precision medicine with human centric generative AI

project-description.description:
The convergence of artificial intelligence with the growing abundance of medical data has the potential to revolutionize the medical landscape. The shift to precision medicine is currently hindered by a lack of technological advancements and integration of diverse medical data. 
Aignostics, a spin-off from Charité Berlin, is developing RudolfVX - a large-scale multimodal foundation model for pathology, capable of leading the way to improved disease diagnosis, better therapy decisions and accelerated drug development. Emerging as the first of its kind in the EU, this sophisticated AI model is capable of creating valuable insights from multiple data types including clinical reports, omics data, and medical images. The model leverages artificial neural networks and self-supervised learning, minimizing data annotation limitations and optimizing computational efficiency. RudolfVX is set to transform pathology and healthcare by integrating generative AI solutions with a human-centric focus, pioneering new possibilities in the field. These downstream applications will stem from a transparent model, fully compliant with EU values in the AI domain. Our solution will enable improved patient outcomes, reduced healthcare costs, and will address the high failure rates in traditional drug development. With RudolfVX, Aignostics will strengthen Europe’s position and become a market leader in computational pathology, offering significant potential in precision medicine and healthcare advancements.

project-title.title: Multimodal Foundation Model for Breast Cancer
Multimodal Foundation Model for Breast Cancer

project-description.description:
Recent advances in deep learning led to the availability of annotated medical datasets for several tasks and modalities, which are traditionally used to train task- and modality-specific models. Our key idea is to leverage the complementary information present in different datasets to pre-train a single large model in a self-supervised way, able to generalize and adapt better to downstream tasks, i.e. a Multimodal Foundation Model (MFM) for breast cancer-related tasks.

Our model will be trained in public and private multimodal datasets (e.g. CT, ultrasound, text, x-ray), different tasks (classification, detection, segmentation, risk, text generation), tested in real data, and will be open-source.

items.abstract: <jats:p>HONeYBEE (Harmonized ONcologY Biomedical Embedding Encoder) is an open-source framework that integrates multimodal biomedical data for oncology applications. It processes clinical data (structured and unstructured), whole-slide images, radiology scans, and molecular profiles to generate unified patient-level embeddings using domain-specific foundation models and fusion strategies. These embeddings enable survival prediction, cancer-type classification, patient similarity retrieval, and cohort clustering. Evaluated on 11,400+ patients across 33 cancer types from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), clinical embeddings showed the strongest single-modality performance with 98.5% classification accuracy and 96.4% precision@10 in patient retrieval. They also achieved the highest survival prediction concordance indices across most cancer types. Multimodal fusion provided complementary benefits for specific cancers, improving overall survival prediction beyond clinical features alone. Comparative evaluation of four large language models revealed that general-purpose models like Qwen3 outperformed specialized medical models for clinical text representation, though task-specific fine-tuning improved performance on heterogeneous data such as pathology reports.</jats:p>
